subject: Auriga integration compatibility brief / architecture Qs
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@auriga.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: integrations@auriga.com, Daniel Reed <dan.reed@auriga.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership intake — baseline infra + test needs

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for taking this on. Per our discovery call we need a brief technical compatibility review before we proceed to a joint POC. High-level constraints from our side:

- Multi-tenant SaaS: no cross-customer data leakage; strict per-tenant KV isolation.
- On-prem connector: some customers will require VPC-to-VPC peering and egress controls.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 120ms for single-turn prompts at 2k tokens.
- Token budget: peak burst to 120 QPS, steady-state 40 QPS.

We attached our network diagram and an initial spreadsheet of inference requirements. Can Redwood provide a recommended reference architecture (hosted + dedicated fallback) and a short test matrix we can validate against our staging tenants? Also please call out any cryptographic or KMS constraints we should be aware of for Private deployments.

Attachment stubs: auriga_network_diagram.pdf (pdf), auriga-inference-requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Marta Lopez
Sr. Solutions Architect, Auriga Inc.
---
Auriga Inc. | auriga.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@auriga.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership intake — baseline infra + test needs

Marta —

Appreciate the details and the artifacts. Quick read-through: your constraints map cleanly to two viable reference flows we typically present:

1) Hosted-first with Dedicated reserved capacity for peak bursts
   - Primary traffic handled by Redwood hosted inference (fastest time-to-value).
   - Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) handles sustained per-tenant throughput and isolates heavy tenants.
   - Smart routing policy: route by tenant SLA, fallback to lower-cost model variant when capacity constrained.

2) Private VPC deployment (for regulated customers)
   - Private control plane + customer VPC; HSM/KMS integration for key material.
   - On-prem connector for low-latency access and egress controls.

Questions / items we'll include in the formal brief:
- Can you share a sample tenant volume profile (QPS by tenant) and a worst-case concurrent KV state size?
- Any customers that require air-gapped deployments (no egress) or particular CCPA/Schrems constraints?

I'm attaching a short compatibility checklist we use for partner validations — it covers model compatibility, quantization options, recommended batching windows, and telemetry hooks we need for per-route observability.

Next steps: Sergio will propose a compact test matrix (latency, throughput, KV-isolation, failover) and a candidate schedule. Can you confirm Auriga's staging window availability next week (July 23–27)?

Attachment stub: redwood-compatibility-checklist.md (md)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@auriga.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership intake — baseline infra + test needs

Marta / team —

Draft test matrix (short):

- Latency SLOs:
  * Single-turn 512 tokens — target p95 < 80ms (hosted), <120ms (private)
  * Multi-turn 2k tokens — target p95 < 160ms (hosted), <200ms (private)

- Throughput / Stability:
  * Ramp test: 0 -> 120 QPS over 10 minutes; sustained 30 minutes at 120 QPS
  * Batching stress: 8 concurrent long-sequence requests with artificial batching windows

- Isolation / Correctness:
  * KV isolation: tenant A writes keys; tenant B attempts reads — confirm no leakage
  * Model variant fallback: simulate capacity loss to validate automatic regional fallback

- Security / KMS:
  * Key rotation test with a simulated KMS failover window
  * TLS mutual auth + client cert rotation acceptance test

Logistics:
- We can run the staged tests in your sandbox on July 24 (09:00–13:00 PT). We'll need: test tenant credentials (short-lived tokens), a network ACL that permits our test harness, and a shared Drive link to your sandbox topology.

I recommend we keep the initial POC focused — run the latency and isolation tests first, then the throughput ramp if those pass. If you want, we can include a short run of quantized model variants (int8) to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Action items I own: produce a 1-page runbook with exact API calls and payloads. Kimberly: I'll sync with you on model variant recommendations.

— Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@auriga.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Reed <dan.reed@auriga.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jul 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership intake — baseline infra + test needs

Thanks — this is helpful and aligned with what we expected. Quick confirmations:

- Sandbox availability: July 24 confirmed (09:00–13:00 PT).
- We've uploaded our network diagram and a short tenant-volume CSV to the Drive folder you listed.
- We have two tenants that will require dedicated Private deployments later in calendar Q4; for the POC we'll test with a single staging tenant.

Two clarifying questions before Sergio's runbook:
1) For quantized variants, does Redwood recommend running int8 on dedicated nodes only, or is hosted int8 supported with the same fallbacks?
2) Our compliance team flagged that for Private deployments we need KMS audit logs exported to our SIEM (Splunk). Can Redwood confirm available export endpoints and expected retention?

Attachment stub: auriga_network_diagram_updated.pdf (pdf)

If you can answer the two items above in the runbook or call on Monday, we'll be set to proceed.

Best regards,
Marta Lopez
Sr. Solutions Architect, Auriga Inc.
